title: Bump the pinned Bun from 1.3.14 to 1.4.0+ (packageManager, .bun-version, the strict-check action, and release.yml's qualification assertion)
description:
Filed at opum-agent's request (cross-session, 2026-09-29), citing quest-cli's QCLI-411 and OPAG-734: Bun 1.3.14 silently strips a top-level binding named `declare` in .ts files, fixed upstream by oven-sh/bun#31239, an ancestor of bun-v1.4.0 and not of 1.3.14. lore and quest release as a pair, so both sides should carry the bump before the release that ships it.

SCOPE, measured in this checkout on 2026-09-29 rather than taken from the relay: the pin is not one field. Six sites.
1. `.bun-version` = 1.3.14 — the floor the shared composite action reads (`bun-version-file: .bun-version` in `.github/actions/setup-bun/action.yml`), used across ci.yml, release.yml and upstream-backlog-watch.yml.
2. `package.json` — `packageManager: bun@1.3.14`.
3. `.github/actions/strict-check/action.yml:18` — hardcoded `bun-version: 1.3.14`; the action is consumed by other repositories pinned to a full commit SHA, so a bump changes what a published revision carries.
4. `.github/workflows/release.yml:363` — a release-time assertion, `if [ "$actual_bun" != "1.3.14" ]` then "::error::Ladybug qualification requires Bun 1.3.14" and exit 1. It reads the version through setup-bun, so bumping the pin without this line breaks the release job: the two move together, and this is the site that fails only during a release. Whether the Ladybug qualification genuinely requires 1.3.14 or the line is a pin snapshot is a question to answer, not assume.
5. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:206,235` — a retry workaround for the known Bun 1.3.14 Linux epoll runtime race; evaluate removing it once the floor moves.
6. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:428-443` — `config test (newest Bun)` runs `latest` on purpose to catch drift between the pinned floor and newest Bun; its comment already records a 1.3.14-to-1.4.x TOML-parser divergence, so it should keep working and may narrow its differential.

NOT URGENT HERE, measured rather than assumed: no top-level binding literally named `declare` exists in src/, test/ or scripts/ — the only occurrences are ordinary `export declare` ambient declarations in scripts/promote-latest.d.mts — so this repository does not carry the live hazard QCLI-411 fixes. This is currency and pair-drop alignment, not a defect fix.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Bun is pinned at 1.4.0 or later everywhere the pin lives — .bun-version, package.json packageManager, and .github/actions/strict-check/action.yml — and a tracked-file grep finds the old version only in historical records (docs/log.md, CHANGELOG.md, .quest/)
release.yml qualification assertion accepts the new version, or records why the qualification host genuinely requires 1.3.14; the release job does not fail on the version check
bun.lock is regenerated with the new Bun and bun install --frozen-lockfile --linker=isolated succeeds under it
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0 under the new pinned Bun on the change own CI run

plan: 1. Pin bun 1.4.2 at every site: .bun-version, package.json packageManager, .github/actions/strict-check/action.yml.
2. release.yml qualification assertion: update to the new pin (the line reads .bun-version through setup-bun and fails only during a release).
3. ci.yml: evaluate the 1.3.14 epoll retry workaround; leave config-test-newest-bun as the floor-vs-newest differential.
4. Regenerate bun.lock under bun 1.4.2 and confirm --frozen-lockfile --linker=isolated still installs.
5. Check the Bun.Glob dot-directory behaviour the orchestrator flagged against lore own globbing (.lore/agents is a dotted path).
6. Gates under 1.4.2: bun test, bun run lore check, bun run lore agents --check.
7. reviewer pass before landing (CLAUDE.md: release.yml changes get one), then PR and close.
implementationNotes:
SCOPE CORRECTION to the filing, measured rather than inherited: this task said six pin sites. The real surface is wider, and DEVELOPMENT.md already carried the authoritative procedure under 'Bumping the pin' -- .bun-version, package.json (packageManager, engines.bun, @types/bun), the digest-pinned Docker E2E base, and any qualification constants or strict-action pins. Sweeping for the old version found, beyond the six: package.json's @types/bun and engines.bun, docker/e2e/Dockerfile (base image + digest), the Ladybug qualification constants in benchmark/ladybug/run.ts (LADYBUG_BENCHMARK_QUALIFICATION_BUN_VERSION) and benchmark/ladybug/package-qualification.ts (two literals), release.yml's SECOND assertion (the concurrency-evidence check at ~:550, not just the qualification-host one at ~:363), README.md's composite-action paragraph, DEVELOPMENT.md, docs/reference/tech-stack.md's runtime/storage row, and four test files that pin the literals or feed fixtures through them (ladybug-benchmark-report, ladybug-benchmark-workflow, ladybug-package-qualification, ladybug-qualification-evidence). No workflow pins inline: every job that needs bun goes through ./.github/actions/setup-bun, which reads .bun-version -- checked per workflow, so quest-cli's missed tracker-integrity.yml has no analogue here.

MEASUREMENTS TAKEN, not relayed. (1) The bug is NOT what the relay said. OPAG-734 reached this session as 'silently strips a top-level binding named declare'; a plain top-level const named declare works fine on BOTH runtimes (measured). oven-sh/bun#31239 is a PARSER SCOPE DESYNC when a TS contextual keyword -- declare, type, abstract, namespace, module, global, interface -- STARTS A LARGER EXPRESSION: the issue's repro exits 133 (SIGTRAP, panic, no output) on 1.3.14 and 0 on 1.4.2, both re-measured here on the identical input. That is the shape test/bun-declare-binding.test.ts pins, and it is the reason the floor moved. (2) Bun.Glob: '.github/workflows/*' returns 0 matches on 1.3.14 and 4 on 1.4.2 with dot: true giving 4 on both -- reproduced in this checkout; no lore test or doc depends on the old behaviour, so it is a behaviour change worth the CHANGELOG line rather than a repair. (3) The Docker digest method was controlled: querying the registry for 1.3.14 reproduces the digest already pinned in the Dockerfile, so the 1.4.2 digest is derived the same way. (4) The epoll retry in ci.yml is KEPT, not deleted: its two observations were taken on the old floor and no one has re-measured the race on 1.4.2, so the comment now says exactly that instead of claiming a same-version bug.
